question: Which Indian author was awarded the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize for 'The Room on the Roof' in 1957, a book which he wrote at the age of 17?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Ruskin Bond.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ruskin Bond wrote the novel **The Room on the Roof**. It was **Bond's first attempt** at writing. 
 
• Bond wrote the novel when he was **seventeen **and won the** John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957.**
 
• In **1992,** he received the** Sahitya Akademi Award** for his novel in English, **Our Trees Still Grow in the Dehra**.
 
• Bond has published a large number of** short stories, essays, novels, and children's books**.
 
• In **1999**, he received the** Padma Shri**, and in **2014, the Padma Bhushan.**
 
• Ruskin Bond's **latest** book, "**A Little Book of India: Celebrating 75 Years of Independence**," which draws on his own experiences and impressions of India, pays respect to the country that has been his home for** 84 years.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salman Rushdie**__

 __
 
• ​Sir Ahmed Salman Rushdie is an **Indian-born British-American **novelist and essayist.
 
• His book "**Midnight's Children"**, **won three Booker prizes.**
 
 
 
• **​Khushwant Singh**__
 __
 
• He was an Indian** politician, author, lawyer, journalist, and diplomat**.
 
• In **1956**, he wrote **Train to Pakistan**, which became his most well-known novel, based on his experiences during the **1947 Partition of India.**
 
• He was most recognized as a writer for his **trenchant secularism, wit, sarcasm,** and a lifelong** love of poetry.**
 
• Between **1980 and 1986**, he was a **Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha**, India's upper house of Parliament.
 
• Khushwant Singh received the **Padma Bhushan in 1974** but returned it in **1984** in protest of the** Indian Army's raid on Amritsar** during **Operation Blue Star**.
 
• In **2007**, he received the** Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian honour.
 
 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh**​__
 
 
• ​Amitav Ghosh is an** Indian author** best recognized for his **historical fiction written in English.**
 
• In** 2018,** he received India's top literary distinction, the** 54th Jnanpith award. **In **1986**, he published his debut novel, "**The Circle of Reason**". The Shadow Lines, The Glass Palace, and the Ibis trilogy are among his later fictional works.
 
• The President of India awarded him the** Padma Shri** in **2007.**
 
• In **2010**, he shared a **Dan David prize** with** Margaret Atwood***,* and in **2011,** he received the** Grand Prix of the Blue Metropolis festival** in Montreal.
